TextBlock.Text: THEATRE North of Tawi-Tawi
DATE 15 October 2028 · 0140 local
SIDE Philippine Navy
WINDOW 110 min, closes at 165
Jacinto class patrol vessel. Photo: National Security Council of the Philippines · Public domain · cropped
"It's not enough to talk about deterrence: I believe we must demonstrate that we can deliver air power to degrade, disrupt, destroy, and defeat."
- Air Marshal Stephen Chappell, Chief of Air Force, RAAF, 2026

SULU SEA, NORTH OF TAWI-TAWI, 0140, flat calm and no moon. The Drug Enforcement Agency has a source in Sandakan who says a semi-submersible left the Sabah coast at dusk with a load for Tawi-Tawi: the kind of cargo that pays for what Meridian is putting ashore on Jolo. She sits a foot out of the water and makes thirteen knots.

The Navy's Tawi-Tawi patrol group has the night. BRP Emilio Jacinto is north-east of the route, BRP Jose Loor Sr. and BRP Juan Magluyan are working the fishing grounds to the west and north, and the Navy's helicopter is up out of Sanga-Sanga. About six fishing boats are out tonight, and the Bongao ferry is on its usual run.

Two fast boats are waiting off the north coast of Tawi-Tawi to take the load. A civilian AS350 has been circling the route since midnight; it is chartered, it is unarmed and it is watching for you. Weapons are Free on the semi-submersible and the pickup boats once classified. Nothing else.
COMMAND NET: A mission-specific tactical report follows eight minutes after the start. It is advice from the command team, not a new sensor detection.
Naval Forces Western Mindanao; Philippine Drug Enforcement Agency liaison
COMMANDER'S INTENT

Find the semi-submersible and stop her before she reaches the coast and the boats waiting for her. She is low, slow and quiet and will be in among the fishing fleet; the helicopter overhead is a charter the runners pay to watch for us. Take the boats too if you can. Harm no fisherman: they are the people this is for.
• Stop the semi-submersible before she reaches the Tawi-Tawi coast
• Classify the semi-submersible
• Stop the pickup boats
• Classify the runners' spotter helicopter
• Harm no fishing boat, ferry or civilian aircraft

The Tawi-Tawi patrol group: BRP Emilio Jacinto, the patrol boats Jose Loor Sr. and Juan Magluyan, and the Navy helicopter Tawi 21 out of Sanga-Sanga. Opposing: one semi-submersible, two pickup boats and a chartered civilian AS350. Neutral: six fishing boats and the Bongao-Zamboanga ferry.

The planned window is 110 minutes. At that minute Command signals that you are behind schedule and holds the line for about 55 minutes more; the operation is closed at 165 minutes and the main task will be recorded as failed.
RULES OF ENGAGEMENT
All designated neutral contacts are protected. A protected neutral loss cancels the operation. Identify before you shoot.
